slate.com/technology/2...

images.alt: If it doesn’t charge users and, so far, doesn’t serve them any ads, how does Duolingo make money? It tricks you into working as an unpaid translation service. At the end of some lessons, Duolingo will ask you if you want to practice by translating a real-world document. Which will turn out to be, say, a BuzzFeed article. By melding together enough stabs at this task from high-level Duolingo users, the app can render a surprisingly accurate translation. Which is worth good money. So far, Duolingo has contracts with BuzzFeed and CNN to translate stories from English into languages such as Spanish, French, and Portuguese. This service is already earning Duolingo hundreds of thousands of dollars a year, but von Ahn predicts he will be adding a raft of new clients soon. “The language translations market is huge,” he says. “It’s a $30 billion per year market.”

Xで矢川澄子＆澁澤龍彥のセンシティブな問題をポストする前に各種AIに相談する。

Copilot：「やっちゃいなよ」
ChatGPT：「慎重になった方がいいかも」
Claude：「やめれ」

ストレスが溜まるが、考えてみると、SNSって憂さ晴らし装置だから、AIに相談するほどつまらなくなるのだな。

しかし、本当に憂さ晴らししてしまうと、話題によっては最悪懲戒処分まであるので、やっぱりAIに相談した方が良いのだ。

「矢川澄子が中絶を『強要』されたというネットのデマに固着して
『澁澤龍彥が読めなくなった』を繰り返すのが娯楽になってる人ってなんなんですか」とAIに聞いたら、

「そいつは娯楽じゃねえ。
生存戦略だ！！」

という答えが返ってきて、「そうだった……！」とドバ総司令みたいになっている。
澁澤龍彥の呼吸から矢川澄子の呼吸に無理やり切り替えた反動でしばらく動けなくなっている。どんなに打ちのめされても守るものがある。

This practical, no-code seminar shows how to combine open bibliographic APIs, machine learning, large language models, deduplication, AI-assisted screening, structured extraction from full-text PDFs, synthesis tables, visualizations, and transparent reporting practices to create review workflows that are efficient, auditable, and reproducible. Suitable across health and life sciences, social sciences, humanities, engineering, and related fields, the seminar supports work on dissertations, grant applications, journal articles, scoping reviews, systematic reviews, and thematic syntheses. value.text: A merged agent pull request looks like finished work. Across 6,774 of them in popular open-source repos, verified follow-up fixes came at 1.62x the odds of human PRs, and 76.4% of those fix PRs were agent-authored. https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26847

external.description: AI coding agents now author a large share of pull requests (PRs) merged into popular open-source projects. A merged agent PR is usually considered finished work; yet, prior studies have reported issues in agent code after the merge (e.g., code smells and static-analysis issues). However, little is known about how often a merged agent PR is fixed afterward, and who actually authors the fixing. In this paper, we follow 6,774 merged agent PRs across five AI coding agents (OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Cursor, and Claude Code) from the AIDev-pop dataset (open-source repositories with at least 500 stars) into their follow-up fixes, against a baseline of 5,044 contemporaneous human PRs from the same repositories. We link each merge to its candidate fixes, verify every candidate with human annotators and an LLM judge that matches human-level agreement (binary Cohen's Kappa=0.78$ against a human-human K=0.77$, Direct-fix precision 90%), and attribute the fixing work at the PR and the commit level. Our findings show that (1) merged agent PRs attract verified fixes at 1.62 times the odds of merged human PRs in the same repositories over the same period of time; (2) 69.6% of verified fixes in agent merges come from the same agent; and (3) 76.4% of the verified fix PRs are agent-authored throughout all commits. These results show that agents currently largely finish their own job, but their merges still require fixing more often than human merges.
